name: Propolis
short: A known contact allergen: 1.2 to 6.6% of people patch-tested for dermatitis react to it. One oral trial found adverse events similar to placebo; a case report describes acute kidney failure.
text: Propolis is a recognised cause of allergic contact dermatitis: a review reported that 1.2 to 6.6% of patients patch-tested for dermatitis are sensitive to it, and that it is found in products such as lip balms, cosmetics, ointments and toothpastes. For propolis taken by mouth, a 24-week double-blind randomised trial of Brazilian propolis tablets in 80 women with rheumatoid arthritis recorded adverse events in 28% of the propolis group and 33% of the placebo group. On the other side, a single case report describes a 59-year-old man with bile duct cancer who developed acute kidney failure needing dialysis after taking propolis for 2 weeks; kidney function improved when he stopped, worsened on re-exposure and recovered after stopping again, and the authors noted that systemic toxicity is rarely reported and may be underestimated. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
